It so chanced, that after the Parsee’s disappearance, I was he whom the Fates ordained to take the place of Ahab’s bowsman, when that bowsman assumed the vacant post; the same, who, when on the last day the three men were tossed from out of the rocking boat, was dropped astern. So, floating on the margin of the ensuing scene, and in full sight of it, when the halfspent suction of the sunk ship reached me, I was then, but slowly, drawn towards the closing vortex. When I reached it, it had subsided to a creamy pool. Round and round, then, and ever contracting towards the button-like black bubble at the axis of that slowly wheeling circle, like another Ixion I did revolve. Till, gaining that vital centre, the black bubble upward burst; and now, liberated by reason of its cunning spring, and, owing to its great buoyancy, rising with great force, the coffin life-buoy shot lengthwise from the sea, fell over, and floated by my side. Buoyed up by that coffin, for almost one whole day and night, I floated on a soft and dirgelike main. The unharming sharks, they glided by as if with padlocks on their mouths; the savage sea-hawks sailed with sheathed beaks. On the second day, a sail drew near, nearer, and picked me up at last. It was the devious-cruising Rachel, that in her retracing search after her missing children, only found another orphan.

modern_en.title: Epilogue — The Drama's Done
paragraphs: "AND I ONLY AM ESCAPED ALONE TO TELL THEE" — Job.
The drama's done. Why then does anyone step forth here? Because one did survive the wreck.

It happened that after the Parsee disappeared, I was the one the Fates appointed to take the place of Ahab's bowsman, when that bowsman took over the vacant post; and I was the same man who, on the last day, when the three men were thrown out of the rocking boat, was dropped astern. So, floating on the edge of the scene that followed, and in full view of it, I was drawn, though slowly, toward the closing vortex when the half-spent suction of the sunken ship reached me. By the time I reached it, it had settled into a creamy pool. Then round and round I went, like another Ixion, always drawing closer to the button-like black bubble at the center of that slowly wheeling circle. At last, when I reached that vital center, the black bubble burst upward; and now, set free by its ingenious spring and rising with great force because of its great buoyancy, the coffin life-buoy shot lengthwise out of the sea, fell over, and floated beside me. Kept afloat by that coffin for almost a whole day and night, I drifted on a soft, dirge-like sea. The sharks glided by without harming me, as if they had padlocks on their mouths; the savage sea-hawks sailed with their beaks sheathed. On the second day a sail drew near, nearer, and picked me up at last. It was the Rachel, cruising her winding course, who in retracing her search after her missing children found only another orphan.

modern_da.title: Epilog — Dramaet er forbi
paragraphs: »OG JEG ALENE ER UNDSLUPPET FOR AT FORTÆLLE DIG DET« — Job.
Dramaet er slut. Hvorfor træder da nogen frem her? Fordi én overlevede vraget.

Det var sådan, at efter at parseren var forsvundet, var det mig, skæbnegudinderne udpegede til at overtage pladsen som Ahabs bådsmand, da han overtog den ledige post. Og jeg var den samme mand, som på den sidste dag, da de tre mænd blev slynget ud af den vuggende båd, blev kastet agterud. Så mens jeg drev i udkanten af scenen, der fulgte, og i fuld udsigt til den, blev jeg langsomt trukket mod den lukkende hvirvel, da det halvt udtømte sug fra det sunkne skib nåede mig. Da jeg nåede den, havde den lagt sig til en flødeagtig pøl. Så rundt og rundt gik jeg som en anden Ixion og kom hele tiden tættere på den knapagtige sorte boble i midten af den langsomt kredsende ring. Til sidst, da jeg nåede det livsvigtige midtpunkt, sprang den sorte boble opad. Nu, sat fri af sin snilde fjeder og stigende med stor kraft på grund af sin store opdrift, skød kistelivbøjen på langs op af havet, væltede og flød ved siden af mig. Holdt oppe af den kiste i næsten et helt døgn drev jeg på et blidt, klagesangsagtigt hav. Hajerne gled forbi uden at gøre mig noget, som om de havde hængelåse for munden. De vilde havhøge sejlede med skedede næb. Den anden dag kom et sejl nærmere, nærmere og samlede mig endelig op. Det var Rachel, som krydsede i sin snoede kurs og i sin søgen efter sine forsvundne børn kun fandt endnu et forældreløst.
